safety.text: Her campaign says neighborhood safety should combine prevention, law enforcement, and mental-health support.
safety.quote: Prevention, law enforcement, and mental health support working together.

health.text: Obeso-Martinez, a nurse practitioner, criticized cuts to Medicaid coverage in her district and pledged to fight for families' health coverage.
health.quote: When the Trump Administration eliminated Medicaid coverage for hundreds of thousands of families across our Desert and Inland communities, our elected Assemblyman was silent.

tax.text: Gonzalez introduced AB 1745 to suspend California's roughly 61-cent-per-gallon gas tax for one year to ease costs on drivers.
tax.quote: This is about affordability, this is about fairness. This is about putting people before politics

schools.text: His platform calls for hiring more teachers and improving school resources and safety.
schools.quote: His platform also calls for eliminating taxes on groceries, passing what he describes as a major middle-class tax cut, hiring more teachers, and strengthening school safety.

safety.text: Gonzalez authored AB 2701, which would have created a public domestic violence offender registry to track and publicize convicted offenders.
safety.quote: AB 2701 was about protecting victims, increasing awareness, and holding the most dangerous offenders accountable

sentencing.text: Joined Republican colleagues in urging the parole board not to release a convicted child molester and emphasized the lasting harm to victims.
sentencing.quote: Joining Republican colleagues at a March 2026 press conference urging the parole board to deny release to a convicted child molester

immigration.text: Justified a troop deployment in Los Angeles while also signing a letter advocating a legal-status pathway for undocumented immigrants.
immigration.quote: He sought to justify Trump’s deployment of troops in Los Angeles last year as “stepping up.” He also signed a caucus letter to Congress last year advocating for a path for legal status for undocumented immigrants.

health.text: Gonzalez says he fought the governor's proposed cuts to In-Home Supportive Services, a publicly funded care program for vulnerable residents.
health.quote: fighting back against the governor when he wanted to cut $700 million dollars from in-home supportive services for the most vulnerable people
